description: Get back to basics with this easy meatloaf recipe. Made with simple ingredients, it comes together quickly, and tastes delicious. Perfect for busy weeknights.
done_temperature: 160 degrees F (70 degrees C) in the middle, instant-read thermometer
steps: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Combine ground beef, onion, milk, bread crumbs, and egg in a large bowl, and season with salt and pepper. Press mixture evenly into the prepared loaf pan.
Stir ketchup, brown sugar, and mustard together in a small bowl until smooth, and spread evenly over the meatloaf.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the middle reads at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).
storage: Refrigerate tightly wrapped or in an airtight container for 3 to 4 days. To freeze, wrap in at least one layer of storage wrap followed by at least one layer of foil, place in a zip-top freezer bag labeled with the date, and freeze for 3 to 4 months.
title: Easy Meatloaf

description: Straightforward and rewarding New York style bagels with a crisp, golden crust and a perfectly chewy interior. Makes 6 large or 9 small bagels.

ingredients.text: 2 1/4 teaspoon instant yeast (7 grams or 1 packet)
4-6 cups water - enough to fill a wide pan about halfway
2 tablespoon barley malt syrup, honey or brown sugar - optional

pan: Baking sheet lined with parchment paper
steps: Make the bagel dough. In a stand mixer bowl, add the water, yeast, and sugar. Stir to combine. Add the flour and salt. Run the mixer with the dough hook attachment on medium-low speed until the dough comes together. Knead for 8-10 minutes. Alternatively, use a large bowl to mix the ingredients and knead the dough on a clean work surface like your countertop until it is supple.
Rise. Shape the dough into a ball and place it in a large lightly oiled bowl. Cover with a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

Divide. Punch the dough down to release trapped air. Divide into 6 equal pieces (for large bagels) or 9 pieces (for smaller bagels) and roll each piece into a ball. Rest on the counter for 10 minutes.

Shape. Poke a hole in the center of each dough ball using your index finger, then gently stretch the dough ball using your index fingers to form a ring. Aim for uniform shaped bagels to ensure even baking.

Boil. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper and sprinkle on some of the topping (this will form the bottom crust). Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the optional 2 tablespoon barley malt syrup, honey or brown sugar. Boil the bagels in batches for 1-2 minutes per side. Use a slotted spoon to remove the boiled bagels and place them on the prepared baking sheet on top of the desired topping.
Brush and dress. While the bagels are still wet and tacky from boiling, brush them with egg wash and sprinkle your chosen toppings.
Bake. Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until they turn golden brown and crisp. Let them cool slightly before enjoying.
storage: Store at room temperature in a paper bag for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them. Slice the bagels before freezing for easy toasting.
title: New York Style Bagel
